title: Affine Gabber effacement (Stacks 09ZE)
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal; put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $i:Z\to X$ be the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] induced by $A\to A/I$ (every closed subscheme of the affine scheme $X$ is of this form). Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] on $X_{\Et}$, i.e. a torsion object of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $q>0$ and let $\xi\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F)$ be a class of etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] of the inverse image $i^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then there are a torsion abelian sheaf $F'$ on $X_{\Et}$ and a monomorphism $\iota:F\to F'$ of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ such that $H^q(i^{-1}\iota)(\xi)=0$ in $H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F')$, where $H^q(\varphi)$ is the map induced on cohomology by a morphism of sheaves $\varphi$ [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. (This is Stacks' statement: $X$ affine, $Z\subseteq X$ any closed subscheme; no henselian hypothesis is needed. In particular it holds for every henselian pair $(A,I)$ and for $I=0$, $Z=X$, $i=\mathrm{id}$, the two cases used in the proof of Gabber's theorem 09ZI.)

proof.text: *$X$ and $Z$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.* $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ are affine; applying [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] to the identity morphisms of $X$ and of $Z$ (affine targets, quasi-compact and separated) shows that both schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (label lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 14900, proof (the lemmas 03SA, 03Q5 and 09Z7 it cites are stated for quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes)

proof.text: *$\xi$ comes from a constructible sheaf (Stacks: 'By Lemmas 03SA and 03Q5 we can find a map $\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal G$ constructible and $\xi$ coming from an element $\zeta$').* (a) $F$ is torsion, so $F=\varinjlim_nF[n]$, the filtered colimit over the positive integers ordered by divisibility, with coprojections the inclusions $j_n:F[n]\hookrightarrow F$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. The inverse image $i^{-1}$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], so $(i^{-1}F,(i^{-1}j_n))$ is a colimit of the filtered diagram $n\mapsto i^{-1}F[n]$ in $\Ab(Z_{\Et})$; $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] (Stacks 03Q5) the map $\varinjlim_nH^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F[n])\to H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F)$ induced by the $H^q(i^{-1}j_n)$ is bijective; an element of a filtered colimit of abelian groups comes from some term [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups], so $\xi=H^q(i^{-1}j_n)(\xi_n)$ for some $n\ge1$ and $\xi_n\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}F[n])$. (b) $F[n]$ is killed by $n$, so it is a sheaf of $(\mathbf Z/n)_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] in exactly one way (the constant sheaf of rings $(\mathbf Z/n)_X$ acts through its locally constant sections, and an additive map between abelian sheaves killed by $n$ is $\mathbf Z/n$-linear). $\mathbf Z/n$ is a finite commutative ring and $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible] (Stacks 03SA (3), which is how Stacks proves 03SA (2): 'write $\mathcal F=\bigcup\mathcal F[n]$ ... and apply (3)') $F[n]$ is the colimit of a filtered diagram $\alpha\mapsto G_\alpha$ of constructible sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], with coprojections $c_\alpha:G_\alpha\to F[n]$. The forgetful functor to $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (3), so this is also a filtered colimit of the underlying abelian sheaves, and as in (a) $\xi_n=H^q(i^{-1}c_\alpha)(\zeta)$ for some $\alpha$ and $\zeta\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}G)$, $G:=G_\alpha$. (c) Put $b=j_n\circ c_\alpha:G\to F$, a morphism of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$. Since $i^{-1}$ is a functor and $\varphi\mapsto H^q(\varphi)$ is functorial [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], $H^q(i^{-1}b)(\zeta)=H^q(i^{-1}j_n)(H^q(i^{-1}c_\alpha)(\zeta))=\xi$. So: $G$ is (the underlying abelian sheaf of) a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules, $b:G\to F$ is a morphism of abelian sheaves, and $\xi=H^q(i^{-1}b)(\zeta)$. ($b$ need not be injective; Stacks does not ask for it.)

proof.text: *Reduction to the constructible sheaf by a pushout (Stacks: 'Suppose we can find an injective map $\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ ... Then we can take $\mathcal F'=\mathcal G'\amalg_{\mathcal G}\mathcal F$').* Suppose $a:G\to G'$ is a monomorphism of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ with $G'$ torsion and $H^q(i^{-1}a)(\zeta)=0$ (constructed in steps 4-9). $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ is abelian and has all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]; let $F'=G'\amalg_GF$ be the pushout of $a$ and $b$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with $\iota:F\to F'$ and $b':G'\to F'$, $\iota\circ b=b'\circ a$. (i) $\iota$ is a monomorphism: the pushout of the monomorphism $a$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-pushout-mono]. (ii) $\xi$ dies: by functoriality of $i^{-1}$ and of $H^q$ [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], $H^q(i^{-1}\iota)(\xi)=H^q(i^{-1}(\iota b))(\zeta)=H^q(i^{-1}(b'a))(\zeta)=H^q(i^{-1}b')(H^q(i^{-1}a)(\zeta))=0$. (iii) $F'$ is torsion: $F'$ is the cokernel of $(a,-b):G\to G'\oplus F$ (Homology, Example 05PJ), so $G'\oplus F\to F'$ is an epimorphism, hence locally surjective [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective]: every local section $s\in F'(U)$ is, on the members $V_j$ of an etale covering of $U$, the image of a pair $(g'_j,f_j)\in G'(V_j)\oplus F(V_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] ((1)$\Rightarrow$(2)) $g'_j$ and $f_j$ are each killed by positive integers on the members of etale coverings of $V_j$; refining by the fibre products of the two coverings, $(g'_j,f_j)$, hence $s$, is killed by the product of the two integers locally. So every local section of $F'$ is locally killed by a positive integer, and $F'$ is torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] ((2)$\Rightarrow$(1)). Hence $(F',\iota)$ proves the lemma, and it remains to construct $a$.

proof.text: *Embedding into finite pushforwards of constant sheaves (Stacks: 'By Lemma 09Z7 it suffices to prove the result when $\mathcal F$ is of the form $f_*\underline M$').* $G$ is a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules on the quasi-compact and quasi-separated $X$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-pushforward-embedding] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$ there are $m\ge0$, finite morphisms $f_k:Y_k\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] locally of finite presentation, finite $\mathbf Z/n$-modules $M_k$ ($k=1,\dots,m$) and a monomorphism $e:G\hookrightarrow\bigoplus_{k=1}^mf_{k,*}\underline{M_k}$ of sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules. Pass to underlying abelian sheaves: the forgetful functor is exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (1), so $e$ stays a monomorphism; it is additive, so it preserves the finite biproduct [def-weil-additive-category]; it commutes with the direct images, which are given on both sides by $(f_*E)(W)=E(W\times_XY)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; and the underlying abelian sheaf of the constant sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules $\underline{M_k}$ is the constant abelian sheaf $\underline{M_k}$ with value the finite abelian group $M_k$ [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying]. So in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ we have a monomorphism $e:G\hookrightarrow D=\bigoplus_{k=1}^mD_k$, $D_k=f_{k,*}\underline{M_k}$, with $f_k$ finite of finite presentation and $M_k$ finite abelian groups.

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (label lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 14900, proof, second paragraph, first sentence; Lemma 09Z7 (label lemma-constructible-maps-into-constant-general, line 13028)

proof.text: *Reduction to one summand (Stacks' 'it suffices', written out).* Let $\epsilon_k:D_k\to D$, $p_k:D\to D_k$ be the injections and projections of the biproduct, $\sum_k\epsilon_kp_k=\mathrm{id}_D$ [def-weil-additive-category]. Put $\zeta_D=H^q(i^{-1}e)(\zeta)$ and $\zeta_k=H^q(i^{-1}p_k)(\zeta_D)\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}D_k)$. Suppose that for every $k$ there is a monomorphism $a_k:D_k\to D'_k$ into a torsion sheaf with $H^q(i^{-1}a_k)(\zeta_k)=0$ (steps 6-9). Let $D'=\bigoplus_kD'_k$ with injections $\epsilon'_k$, $a_D=\bigoplus_ka_k:D\to D'$ (so $a_D\epsilon_k=\epsilon'_ka_k$), and $a=a_D\circ e:G\to D'$. $a_D$ is a monomorphism (its kernel is $\bigoplus_k\ker a_k=0$, kernels being computed sectionwise), so $a$ is one. $D'$ is torsion: a local section of $D'$ is a tuple of local sections of the $D'_k$, each locally killed by a positive integer, so the tuple is locally killed by their product [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations]. Finally $i^{-1}$ is additive [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and $\varphi\mapsto H^q(\varphi)$ is additive and functorial [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (a sum of lifts to K-injective resolutions lifts the sum, as in step 6 of lemma-weil-pbc-h1-constructible-representation), so $H^q(i^{-1}a)(\zeta)=H^q(i^{-1}a_D)(\zeta_D)=\sum_kH^q(i^{-1}(a_D\epsilon_kp_k))(\zeta_D)=\sum_kH^q(i^{-1}\epsilon'_k)\bigl(H^q(i^{-1}a_k)(\zeta_k)\bigr)=0$. This $a$ is what step 3 needs.

source.place: Lemma 09ZE (label lemma-efface-cohomology-on-closed-by-finite-cover), etale-cohomology.tex line 14900, proof, second paragraph, first sentence ('it suffices to prove the result when F is of the form f_*M')

proof.text: *The class on the closed fibre of $Y$ (Stacks: 'Since formation of $f_*$ commutes with any base change ... By the Leray spectral sequence and vanishing of higher direct images, $H^q(Z,f_*\underline M|_Z)=H^q(Y\times_XZ,\underline M)$').* Fix $k$ and write $f=f_k:Y\to X$, $M=M_k$, $\zeta_1=\zeta_k\in H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}f_*\underline M)$. $Y$ is affine, being finite over the affine $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (b). Let $Y_Z=Y\times_XZ$ with projections $i_Y:Y_Z\to Y$, a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and $f_Z:Y_Z\to Z$, finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a); regard $\square=(f,f_Z,i,i_Y)$ as a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. The underived exchange morphism $\Ex^0_{\square,\underline M}:i^{-1}f_*\underline M\to f_{Z,*}i_Y^{-1}\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] is an isomorphism since $f$ is finite [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] (Stacks 0959), so $H^q(\Ex^0_{\square,\underline M})$ is bijective (functoriality, [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]); the edge map $e^q_{f_Z,i_Y^{-1}\underline M}:H^q(Z_{\Et},f_{Z,*}i_Y^{-1}\underline M)\to H^q((Y_Z)_{\Et},i_Y^{-1}\underline M)$ is bijective since $f_Z$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] (Stacks 03QP and 03QC). So $\Phi_f=e^q_{f_Z,i_Y^{-1}\underline M}\circ H^q(\Ex^0_{\square,\underline M})$ is an isomorphism $H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}f_*\underline M)\cong H^q((Y_Z)_{\Et},i_Y^{-1}\underline M)$, and $i_Y^{-1}\underline M$ is the constant sheaf $\underline M$ on $Y_Z$ [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Let $\tilde\zeta=\Phi_f(\zeta_1)\in H^q((Y_Z)_{\Et},\underline M)$.

proof.text: *Killing $\tilde\zeta$ by a finite surjective cover (Stacks: 'By Lemma 09ZD we can find a finite surjective morphism $Y'\to Y$ of finite presentation such that $\xi$ maps to zero in $H^q(Y'\times_XZ,\underline M)$').* $Y$ is affine (step 6), $Y_Z\subseteq Y$ is a closed subscheme ($i_Y$ is a closed immersion), $M$ is a finite abelian group and $q\ge1$; by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-cover-kills-constant-cohomology] (Stacks 09ZD (2)) there is a finite surjective morphism of finite presentation $\pi:Y'\to Y$ such that $\tilde\zeta$ pulls back to zero along the projection $Y'\times_YY_Z\to Y_Z$. Let $Y'_Z=Y'\times_XZ$ with projections $i_{Y'}:Y'_Z\to Y'$, $f'_Z:Y'_Z\to Z$, and $\pi_Z=\pi\times_X\mathrm{id}_Z:Y'_Z\to Y_Z$; by the pasting of fibre products $Y'\times_YY_Z=Y'\times_Y(Y\times_XZ)\cong Y'\times_XZ=Y'_Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the projection to $Y_Z$ becoming $\pi_Z$. Hence $\pi_Z^*\tilde\zeta=0$ in $H^q((Y'_Z)_{\Et},\pi_Z^{-1}i_Y^{-1}\underline M)$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] (the identifications of the inverse images of $\underline M$ with constant sheaves are isomorphisms of sheaves, and $\pi_Z^*$ is natural in the sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (3), so vanishing does not depend on them).

proof.text: *The effacing sheaf $f'_*\underline M$ and its injectivity (Stacks: 'Denoting $f':Y'\to X$ the composition we claim the map $f_*\underline M\to f'_*\underline M$ is injective ... look at stalks ... Since $Y'\to Y$ is surjective and finite ...').* $f'=f\circ\pi$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. Put $D'_1=f'_*\pi^{-1}\underline M$ ($\pi^{-1}\underline M$ is the constant sheaf $\underline M$ on $Y'$ [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], so this is Stacks' $f'_*\underline M$) and let $a_1:D_1=f_*\underline M\to D'_1$ be $f_*(\eta_{\pi,\underline M}):f_*\underline M\to f_*\pi_*\pi^{-1}\underline M$ followed by the identification $f_*\pi_*=(f\pi)_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] ($\eta_\pi$ the unit of $\pi^{-1}\dashv\pi_*$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]); on sections it is the pullback $\underline M(W\times_XY)\to\underline M(W\times_XY')$, Stacks' map. $a_1$ is a monomorphism: $\eta_{\pi,\underline M}$ is a monomorphism because $\pi$ is finite and surjective [lem-weil-pbc-finite-surjective-unit-mono] (this is Stacks' stalk computation), and $f_*$ is left exact [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] (a right adjoint), so it preserves monomorphisms. $D'_1$ is torsion: multiplication by $N=|M|$ on $\pi^{-1}\underline M$ is $\pi^{-1}$ of multiplication by $N$ on $\underline M$ ($\pi^{-1}$ is additive [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]), which is $0$ since every section of $\underline M$ takes values in $M$; hence $N$ kills $D'_1(W)=\pi^{-1}\underline M(W\times_XY')$ for every $W$, i.e. $D'_1[N]=D'_1$, and then $D'_1[n]=D'_1$ for all $n$ divisible by $N$, a cofinal set of indices, so $c_{D'_1}:\varinjlim_nD'_1[n]\to D'_1$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf].

proof.text: *The class dies in $D'_1$ (Stacks: '... which finishes the proof by what was said above').* By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-unit-edge-compatibility] applied to $f$, $\pi$, $i$ and $G=\underline M$ (the map $u$ there is $a_1$), $\Phi_{f'}\bigl(H^q(i^{-1}a_1)(\zeta_1)\bigr)=H^q(\kappa)\bigl(\pi_Z^*\Phi_f(\zeta_1)\bigr)=H^q(\kappa)(\pi_Z^*\tilde\zeta)=0$ by step 7, where $\Phi_{f'}:H^q(Z_{\Et},i^{-1}f'_*\pi^{-1}\underline M)\to H^q((Y'_Z)_{\Et},i_{Y'}^{-1}\pi^{-1}\underline M)$ is the map of step 6 for the finite morphism $f'$ and the cartesian square $(f',f'_Z,i,i_{Y'})$. As in step 6, $\Phi_{f'}$ is an isomorphism ([lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-cohomology] for the finite $f'$ and its base change $f'_Z$, finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a)), so $H^q(i^{-1}a_1)(\zeta_1)=0$. Thus $a_k:=a_1$ (for the summand $k$ fixed in step 6) is a monomorphism into a torsion sheaf killing $\zeta_k$; doing this for every $k$ gives the hypothesis of step 5, whose output is the $a$ required in step 3. This proves the lemma.
